dataset.t: Each dot is a customer, placed by **purchases per month** and **average spend**. The groups **overlap**, so some customers sit between groups. Colors have not been assigned yet.

component-center.t: A Gaussian mixture is built from **Gaussian components**. The cross marks one component's **mean**: the center of its cloud of customers.

component-spread.t: Each component also has a **spread**. In two dimensions the **covariance** gives the cloud its size, shape and orientation, here a wide, flat ellipse.

component-weight.t: Each component has a **mixing weight**: the share of customers it accounts for. Across all components the weights **add up to 1**.

three-gaussians.t: Three components A, B and C, each with its **own mean, spread and weight**. Each point is colored by blending the components that explain it.

overlap.t: Between B and C the clouds overlap. A customer there is **plausible under both components**, something a hard one-label method cannot express.

combine-density.t: Now we look at spend alone. The weighted components at 2, 5 and 8 add up to a single **mixture density with three peaks**.

new-point.t: A new customer at spend **3.5**: component A contributes **0.0258**, B contributes **0.0583** and C almost nothing, so the mixture density there is **0.0841**.

gmm-view.t: A GMM describes data with components that each have a **mean, a spread and a weight**. Unlike a K-Means centroid, each component also says **how wide and how large** it is.
